raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I've been working this land for 35 years, so I pretty much know what to do.

I've got 12 mu total. I'll do wheat-maize on 8 mu like always — that's the safe one, we eat the wheat and sell the maize. The other 4 mu I'll put in cotton. Cotton brings in cash but it's a lot of work, my back isn't what it used to be, and the wife helps with picking.

**Wheat (already in the ground from last October, 8 mu):**
The wheat went in around early October, after I cleared the maize. I put down a bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's the 15-15-15 stuff from the agro-shop in town, about one bag for each mu. Now in spring, when it greens up and starts jointing, I'll topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu. That's what my father did, that's what the neighbors do. If the wheat looks yellow I add a bit more, if it looks dark green I hold back.

Water — I'll irrigate maybe 3 times. Once after greening up in March, once at jointing, once at heading. The well is metered now so I can't just leave it running like the old days. Costs money. Harvest end of May or early June when the combine man comes through the village.

**Maize (after wheat, 8 mu):**
Soon as the wheat is off, I have to get the maize in fast — maybe 3-4 days. I'll get the neighbor with the no-till planter to come do it, costs me about 30 yuan per mu but it's worth it because at my age I can't be out there with a hand planter. I use the Zhengdan or Xianyu seed, whatever the shop has — about 4-5 yuan per mu of seed.

For maize I put fertilizer with the seed, the planter does it together. Maybe a bag of compound per mu. Then if it looks like it needs it, I topdress urea once. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat, if the rains come I might not irrigate at all. If July is dry I'll water once or twice.

**Cotton (4 mu):**
Cotton I plant late April. This is the tricky one. I put down a bag of compound before plowing, then mulch with plastic film — the seed goes through the holes. Through the summer I have to spray for bollworm, aphids, the whole thing. That stuff is expensive but if you skip it the cotton is finished. I spray maybe 5-6 times through the season. My son comes back from town to help with picking in September-October, my wife and I can't do it all.

**Money:**
I figure inputs cost me maybe 4,500-5,000 yuan total for the year. That's tight but manageable. If prices are bad on cotton I'll think about going all wheat-maize next year.
